sources.citation: Elizabeth F. Loftus, John C. Palmer (1974). Reconstruction of automobile destruction: An example of the interaction between language and memory. Journal of Verbal Learning and Verbal Behavior.
sources.notes: Foundational primary study (1974) in Journal of Verbal Learning and Verbal Behavior establishing the core experimental paradigm and quantitative parameters.

sources.citation: Julia Shaw, Stephen Porter (2015). Constructing Rich False Memories of Committing Crime. Psychological Science.
sources.notes: Shaw & Porter (2015) rich false memory implantation study.

sources.citation: Elizabeth F Loftus, Jacqueline E Pickrell (1995). The Formation of False Memories. Psychiatric Annals.
sources.notes: Landmark Lost in the Mall study planting false childhood autobiographical episodes in 6 of 24 adults (25%).

sources.citation: Kimberley A. Wade, Maryanne Garry, Kathy Pezdek (2018). Deconstructing Rich False Memories of Committing Crime: Commentary on Shaw and Porter (2015). Psychological Science.
sources.notes: Critical re-scoring of Shaw & Porter (2015) separating genuine perceptual false memories (~26-30%) from false beliefs.

sources.citation: Elizabeth F. Loftus (2005). Planting misinformation in the human mind: A 30-year investigation of the malleability of memory. Learning & Memory.
sources.notes: 30-year synthesis of post-event misinformation, memory malleability, and eyewitness testimony reform.
